statement: Six couples meet at a party. Each person shakes hands once with every other person except their own partner. How many handshakes are there?

choices.misconception: I counted handshakes between all 12 people and forgot that partners do not shake hands.
I took away one handshake for each of the 12 people instead of one for each of the 6 couples.
I said each person shakes 10 hands and multiplied by 12, without halving.
I multiplied 12 by 11 and forgot both to halve and to remove the partners.

hints: How many hands does one person shake?
Handshakes and pairs: count from each person's point of view, then remember that every handshake has two people in it, so that total counts each handshake twice.
Each of the 12 people shakes 10 hands, which gives 120, but each handshake was counted by both people.

solutions.reliable: Each of the 12 people shakes hands with everyone except themselves and their partner, so 10 people. That gives 12 x 10 = 120, but each handshake is counted once by each of the two people, so there are 60 handshakes. The transferable idea: count from each person, then divide by 2 because every pair was counted from both ends.
solutions.elegant: If everyone shook hands, there would be 12 x 11 / 2 = 66 handshakes. Exactly 6 are missing, one per couple, so 66 - 6 = 60.

whyOnTest: Counting pairs with a restriction checks whether you halve correctly and remove the right number of missing pairs.
